title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bradford, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bradford, AR | White County
metaDescription: Own a small gas royalty interest near Bradford, Arkansas? We evaluate White County Fayetteville Shale flank tracts, including thin or marginal interests, and pay cash.
heroLead: Bradford is a small White County town where Fayetteville Shale activity was always thinner than the play's core counties, and interests here often go unmanaged for years.
intro: This part of White County saw leasing activity during the Fayetteville Shale's boom years, but drilling results on the play's eastern flank were generally weaker than closer to Faulkner and Van Buren counties. Many families around Bradford hold small interests that generate modest or no current income, and it's common for nobody to have checked on the status of the lease in years.

sections.heading: Thin gas shows on the eastern flank
paragraphs: Wells drilled near Bradford, where they exist at all, typically produced at lower rates than the Fayetteville Shale's better counties, and many declined to marginal status faster. That's the honest baseline for valuation here, and we price accordingly rather than assuming Bradford acreage carries the same value as core-play tracts.

sections.heading: Interests that haven't generated a check in years
paragraphs: If your family's royalty statements stopped a while back, or never really amounted to much to begin with, that's common in this part of the county. We check current well status and operator filings before telling you what, if anything, the interest is worth today.
In some cases the honest answer is that a specific tract has limited near-term value; in others, there's more there than the family realized because of acreage size or nearby renewed interest.

sections.heading: Confirming what you actually own
paragraphs: We work from your deed, an old lease, or a division order number to confirm your fractional share through White County records before making any offer.

faqs.question: We haven't received a royalty check in a long time. Is our interest dead?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily dead, but it may reflect a shut-in or marginal well. We check current status before concluding anything.

faqs.question: Is Bradford part of the more active core of the Fayetteville Shale?
faqs.answer: No, it's on the eastern flank, which historically produced at lower rates than counties like Faulkner and Van Buren.

faqs.question: Can you still buy a very small fractional interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, small interests are common in this area and we evaluate them the same way we would a larger tract, based on actual production and decline data.

faqs.question: Should we get a second opinion before selling a Bradford-area interest?
faqs.answer: We'd encourage it. Ask us for the production and operator records we used so you can verify the numbers independently before deciding.
